context_for_next_testing_agent: The bug fix uses a small L(ca,es) helper (v2.html line 499). Any future hardcoded string that needs both-language support should use this helper. Do NOT rely on the data-i18n MutationObserver system for strings inside innerHTML template literals — L() is the correct pattern. When testing language switch, use toggleLang() (line 500) directly via page.evaluate, then call render() to refresh sumBox. The isC (currentCompany==='cempla') branch of the sumBox innerHTML still has one hardcoded 'Banco' — see critical_code_review_comments if that becomes a scope item.
rca of the issue: Root cause of Marc's bug: several strings inside JS innerHTML template literals (sumBox fp labels, datafono popup, fp-menu) were hardcoded in Catalan — they never went through the data-i18n dictionary because they are dynamically injected via innerHTML rather than static markup. The MutationObserver-based i18n system only rewrites text nodes matching known ca→es replacements, so any string not in the L() dictionary or applyLang() map stayed in Catalan even when currentLang==='es'. Fix: introduce L(ca,es) helper and wrap each affected string. Verified end-to-end via Playwright against the preview URL for both 'es' (default) and 'ca' modes. All expected strings render correctly in both languages.
